study type: Secondary analysis of a prospective, observational study
exposure: Maternal Breath Carbon Monoxide (BCO) levels at the first antenatal visit
outcome: Neonatal outcomes (emergency caesarean section, low birth weight, birth weight <25th centile, fetal distress, adverse pregnancy events)
cohort: 234 pregnant women aged ≥18 years who delivered a normally formed baby weighing ≥500g
finding: Increased maternal BCO levels at the first antenatal visit were associated with lower birth weight and increased risk of adverse pregnancy and neonatal outcomes.
